disease_label_per_paper: Herpes simplex virus encephalitis involving the right thalamus
presentation_summary: 50-year-old woman was admitted with lethargy, confusion, dysphasia, and cough.
Brain MRI demonstrated bilateral temporal and perisylvian hyperintense signal abnormality extending into the cingulate gyrus, typical of HSV encephalitis.
MRI also showed signal abnormality involving the right thalamus, an uncommon extension for HSV encephalitis.
EEG and CSF PCR confirmed HSV encephalitis.
She received intravenous acyclovir and had marked improvement.
